title: Grease a loader's pivot pin with a lever grease gun without leaking grease at the nipple
instruction: Grease the loader's pivot pin through its grease nipple with the lever grease gun, without leaking any grease at the coupler or the nipple. Leave the coupler back in its holder cup and both arms back where they started.
context: Greasing machine pivots through their grease nipples is routine work for mobile heavy equipment mechanics ("Clean, lubricate, and perform other routine maintenance work on equipment and vehicles", 180,300 US workers) and industrial machinery mechanics ("Clean, lubricate, or adjust parts, equipment, or machinery", 446,900), together about 627,000 (O*NET, 2025), most often with a lever grease gun. A lock-on coupler is pushed squarely over the nipple's ball head with its thumb lever pressed and locks when the lever is let go; it then stays on by itself while the gun's handle is worked, and comes off when the lever is pressed again. Pumping while it is not sealed squarely on squirts grease out at the nipple and leaves the pin dry.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A loader arm's pivot, fixed to the table: a dark steel base plate 12 by 10 cm and 1 cm thick, centred 30 cm forward and 8 cm right; on it a yellow-painted steel lug 5 cm front to back, 4 cm wide and 5.6 cm tall (its top 6.6 cm above the table), with a 20 mm steel pin through its 20.5 mm bore from side to side 3 cm above the table (washers, split pins, and the arm's two yellow steel side plates on it); a 5 mm passage drilled down from the nipple feeds the bore (the passage, the hole under the nipple and the bore's clearance hold about 1.2 cm³). Screwed into the lug's top, a straight grease nipple to DIN 71412 form A: yellow-zinc-plated steel, M10x1 taper thread (5.5 mm long, in the lug), an 11 mm hex 3.5 mm tall, a 4 mm neck and a 6.5 mm ball head whose top is 10.5 mm above the lug (7.65 cm above the table). (2) A lever grease gun lying fixed in a plywood cradle, its axis 33 cm forward: a plated steel barrel 57 mm across, from 18 to 51 cm left with its axis 3.5 cm above the table, and a dark cast head from 10.5 to 18 cm left with the hose outlet on its right face. Its handle, a plated steel bar 30 cm long with a black rubber grip (26 mm wide, 20 mm tall) on its last 11 cm, is pivoted on the head 9 cm above the table and rests level along the top of the barrel, the grip 1.7 cm above it; it opens 60 degrees at most and has no return spring. Lifting it draws grease into the gun; pushing it back down drives grease out, about 0.018 cm³ per degree (a full 53.5-degree stroke is about 0.95 cm³). Its 0.3 kg weighs about 2 N at the grip, and moving it at 17 degrees a second takes about 5 N more there (the grease's resistance); a real rig is checked with a spring scale on the grip to take at most 15 N pushing it down with the coupler locked on. (3) An 18-inch (46 cm) black whip hose, 12 mm across, from the gun's outlet in a loop over the table to (4) a lock-on grease coupler for ball-head nipples, the kind with four hardened steel jaws that lock behind the ball and a thumb lever that opens them (82 g, 4.8 cm tall): a zinc-plated hardened steel nose 18 mm across and 12 mm tall whose closed jaws form a 7.2 mm mouth with a 45-degree lead-in (10.4 mm across at the face) running 5 mm up to a nitrile seal ring 2 mm thick with a 4.6 mm hole; above the nose a black-oxide steel body, 13 mm hex and 2.6 cm tall, with a steel thumb lever (12 g, 6 mm wide and 2 cm long) on its left-facing flat, sprung 2.5 mm out (3 N starts it in, 10.5 N presses it fully in); on top a brass swivel 12 mm across with a 10 mm side outlet where the hose comes in. Pushed fully onto the nipple with its thumb lever out (or let out once it is on), the jaws lock behind the ball head: the seal ring's edge sits on the ball about 1 mm below its top and the nose's face 1 mm above the hex, and the coupler stays there with no hand on it, against the grease pressure, until the thumb lever is pressed in again. Not locked, nothing holds it on. It stands upright in (5) a steel holder cup on a foot plate, centred 24 cm forward on the centre line: 4.6 cm across and 1.6 cm tall, with a 45-degree funnel mouth (4 cm across at the rim) down to a 22 mm seat 3 mm deep that the nose stands in; its steel is smooth, so a coupler set down on the funnel slides into the seat. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. For real trials every finger pad of both grippers wears a disposable nitrile cover, and towel-lined drip trays sit under the pivot, the holder and the gun's outlet (see the README's rig-protection section).
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. Sealed: the ball head fully inside the coupler's mouth with the seal on it: the ball's centre within 1.5 mm of the coupler's axis, the seal within 0.5 mm of the ball's top (at most 1 mm into it), and the coupler tilted at most 8 degrees; a locked coupler is held so by its jaws. (From the real parts: the closed jaws' 7.2 mm mouth leaves 0.35 mm round the 6.5 mm ball, and at about 10 degrees of tilt the nose meets the hex and lifts the seal off the far side of the ball.) A stroke: the gun's handle lifted more than 20 degrees off its stop, then pushed back down to within 3 degrees of it. A shot: a stroke pushed down with the coupler sealed. Leak (latched for the rest of the trial): the gun pushing grease (the handle come down 3 degrees or more from the highest point it was lifted to, and not yet back within 1.5 degrees of its stop) at any moment while the coupler is not sealed on the nipple, whether it sits askew on the nipple or is anywhere else. Greased: at least four shots (each at least about 0.3 cm³, together more than the 1.2 cm³ the pin's passage and bore hold, so fresh grease comes out at both ends of the bore) and no leak; a dab of grease shows at the bore's ends for each of the first four shots, and one shows where a leak happened. In its holder: the coupler's mouth down in the holder cup's seat (within 6 mm of its middle and at most 6 mm above its floor), the coupler tilted less than 35 degrees. 1.0: greased, the coupler in its holder at the end and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: greased at some point; 0.25: the coupler sealed on the nipple at some point; else 0.0. A leak removes the greasing credit (1.0 and 0.5). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the coupler, its thumb lever, the gun's handle and the hose still. In a real trial the same rules are judged from the video and two wipes: wipe the nipple, the bore's ends and the coupler's nose clean first (the bore already full of grease); a card behind the handle marks 20 degrees, and strokes and shots are counted as the handle's grip passes that line and comes back down onto its stop with the coupler on the nipple; sealed means the coupler stays on by itself when let go, or its nose is seen down at the nipple's hex; a leak is grease seen escaping at the coupler or the nipple, or grease on a white cloth wiped round the nipple's hex and the outside of the coupler's nose afterwards. After four shots a white cloth wiped over both ends of the bore shows fresh grease; if it does not, the rig is at fault and the trial is run again.
reset_notes: Lower the gun's handle onto its stop; stand the coupler back upright in its holder cup with its thumb lever facing left and the hose lying as at the start; wipe the grease off the bore's ends, the nipple and the coupler (the bore stays full of grease), then wipe the coupler's hex body and thumb lever with isopropyl alcohol; change the pad covers if any grease reached them.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). No grease flows: shots are handle strokes through the sealed-seat rule; drawn dabs show grease at the bore or a leak. Rigid seal. The jaws' lock is a joint switched on when the coupler is sealed with its thumb lever (a sprung pad) out. A damper on the handle stands in for the grease's resistance; while the gun pushes grease the task file pushes the coupler off with 21 N. Hose: six segments on ball joints. Cameras 1280 x 704.
